newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, seen up on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, seen up on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares on Wednesday rebounded after four sessions of slight falls and analysts said that despite another likely gain on Thursday, signalled by stronger buying after fixing, the market had little upside.
They said the run-up to September's parliamentary poll and Wednesday's news the central bank would raise nominal rates should dampen buying in the weeks ahead.

"I think some of it (a possible rate rise) has already been discounted, as it has been discussed since the start of the floods, but the moment when the move happens it should cause a non-drastic fall," said Emil Onyszczuk of PBR brokerage. (PBR).

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.8 percent to 15,029.8 and turnover fell 11.8 percent to 134.8 million zlotys ($38.8 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 72 to 18 with 16 stocks flat.

The central bank president told daily Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki in its Wednesday edition lombard and discount rates would rise in the next few weeks and it would start collecting deposits to offset effects of government flood relief credit.
The government may borrow as much as 2.5 billion zlotys ($720 million)from the central bank due to the flooding estimated to have caused damage of billions of dollars.
Optimus rose the daily maximum 10 percent on Wednesday, a surge traders said might be speculative as no significant new information on the firm had been released this week.

They said bank BIG, down 4.1 percent in light trade to 3.5 zlotys ($1), was hurt by Tuesday's news it had sold shares in its issue to help refinance the acquisition of Bank Gdanski at 3.4 zlotys ($0.98) each.
The previous price range was 3.3-5.3 zlotys ($0.95-1.5).
